see: تونل، قهرمان پهلو خوابیده، پیپ در بغل، خاک می‌ریزد
text: Day ten.

see: کلوزآپ صورت با خاک روی آن
text: The ground shakes. Dirt pours from the ceiling of your tunnel.
Outside, the sky is on fire.
And at the door, something too big to fit inside is breathing.
(pause)
Ten days ago, you were asleep in your own bed.
You have 10 days before the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs.
Every big animal you see will die.
You won't. If you stay small.

see: اتاق شب، از در به داخل
text: The night before was like any other.
Homework, a documentary about the dinosaurs,
your phone at 23%. "I'll charge it in the morning."

see: میز کار، کوله‌ی باز رو به دوربین
text: In your backpack, ready for school:
two textbooks, a sandwich, two chocolate bars, half a bottle of water.

see: دست قهرمان کتاب را در کوله می‌گذارد
text: And a library book you wanted to read in the break tomorrow.

see: اینسرت جلد کتاب: اسکلت تی‌رکس موزه (زخم دیده نمی‌شود)
text: The Last Day of the Dinosaurs.
In the morning, there's no ceiling.
There are leaves, each one bigger than your bed.
The air is hot and wet. No cars. No voices.
Next to you, something rises from the ground like a tree trunk.
It isn't a tree. It has claws.
The foot lifts, slams down one step ahead,
and the ground jumps under you.
You don't breathe until the footsteps fade.
Your backpack is lying next to you.
Your phone is still in your pocket. No signal. No internet.
Just one message that wasn't there last night.
"Impact: 10 days. 3,000 kilometers south."
A prank. A dream. It has to be.

see: واید: پسر کوچک در دره، راه می‌افتد (frame-right)
text: You switch it off at 22%, and you start walking.

see: پسر روی صخره، به افق خیره، آسمان خالی
text: All afternoon, you look for a road, a wire, a plane in the sky.

see: از پشت: پسر تنها جلوی جنگل بی‌انتها
text: Anything. There's nothing.
In the evening, you find the owner of the foot.
A T. rex. 12 meters, nose to tail,
with a long pale scar across its snout.
For one second, its head turns toward you.
Then it walks on.
It's not a dream.

see: شب، ریشه‌های غول‌پیکر، پسر لای آن‌ها (مادر)
text: That night you squeeze in between the roots of a giant tree.

see: کلوز: زانو در بغل، چشم‌ها باز
text: You're shaking. You don't want to sleep.
In the dark, you open your backpack, looking for anything that makes sense.
The library book.
On the cover, a T. rex skeleton in a museum. You don't look closely.

see: کتاب باز: نقاشی حیوان‌های کوچک (بدون متن)
text: Inside, chapter seven. Who Survived.

see: سه برش از نقاشی‌های کتاب، پشت سر هم
text: Animals that were small. Animals that hid underground. Animals that lived near fresh water.

see: دست با خودکار روی صفحه‌ی آخر (نوشته محو)
text: On the back page, with your school pen, you write a plan.

see: کلوز صورت لای ریشه‌ها زیر نور چراغ
text: Three things. Ten days. None of them done.
You don't decide to fall asleep. Your body decides for you.
In the morning, there's a small hole by the roots.
A furry face pokes out. Mouse-sized. Sniffs. Disappears.
You name him Pip.
The T. rex needs mountains of meat every day.
Pip needs a few seeds and a hole to hide in.
And your book agrees.
Scientists think that after the impact, almost no land animal heavier than about 25 kilograms survived.
You weigh 70.

see: برش از #62: پسر و پیپ (به‌جای قاب روی شکم)
text: So you'll have to think like Pip.
Rule one: stay small.
You eat half the sandwich. You save the rest.

see: پسر روی ریشه نشسته، پیپ را تماشا می‌کند
text: Then you watch what Pip eats.
Small red berries, seeds from one kind of fern.
That's no guarantee. Plenty of things a mouse can eat would kill you.
But he's a mammal, like you, and the sandwich won't last.

see: اینسرت: یک توت قرمز بین دو انگشت سیاه
text: You eat one berry. You wait. By evening, nothing has happened.

see: دست‌ها جیب را با توت پر می‌کنند
text: You fill your pockets.
Day three. The bottle is empty.
Your throat is burning.
You follow the sound of water to a wide, muddy river.
At the edge, a log is floating.
It blinks.
It isn't a log. It's a crocodile.
So you don't drink from the river.
A few steps back from the bank, in the sand, you dig a pit and wait.
Water seeps in through the sand. Slow. Muddy. But cleaner than the river, and far from the teeth.
You fill the bottle.
In the shallow pools, small fish are trapped.

see: اینسرت: سه ماهی روی سنگ داغ
text: You catch three and dry them on a hot rock.

see: غروب گرم روی رود، مه گرم
text: No fire needed. It's warm here, almost tropical, even at night.
From now on, every morning starts at the pools.

see: لاک‌پشت و قورباغه روی تنه + برچسب‌ها
text: The book says freshwater animals, turtles, frogs, even crocodiles, made it through far better than most.
Rule two: stay near water.
Day four. The ground shakes again. Not one footstep. Hundreds.
A herd of duck-billed dinosaurs comes along the river.

see: پسر دست روی سینه، نگاه به دور
text: Then a deep sound rolls in from far away. You feel it in your chest more than your ears.
The herd panics. Trees snap.
You throw yourself behind a fallen log.
When the dust settles, one of them didn't get up.

see: پسر استخوان کتف را بالا می‌گیرد
text: And it has something you need. A shoulder blade. Flat. Wide. The size of a paddle.
From today, your shovel is a dinosaur.

see: صبح کنار رود، کتاب باز روی زانو، صورت جدی
text: Day five. You read the page you've been avoiding.

see: صفحه‌ی کتاب: نقاشی باران سنگ‌های سوزان روی جنگل (بدون متن)
text: Within an hour of the impact, burning debris falls back through the sky, all over the world.
Scientists still argue about how hot it got. In many places, hot enough to set forests on fire.
On the surface, there's nowhere to hide. Under a meter of soil, maybe.
Rule three: stay underground.

see: پسر با استخوان‌بیل کنار دیواره‌ی رسی
text: You find a clay bank above the river and start digging.

see: ✂️ حذف شد (خط سیل از سناریو برداشته شد)
text: Then you look at the trees.

see: ✂️ حذف شد (خط سیل از سناریو برداشته شد)
text: Every trunk has a band of dried mud on it. As high as your head.

see: ✂️ حذف شد (خط سیل از سناریو برداشته شد)
text: The river floods. Right up to here.

see: ✂️ حذف شد (خط سیل از سناریو برداشته شد)
text: So you start again, higher up the bank. A hand above the line. The afternoon is gone.

see: پسر نشسته، خودکار و کتاب، حساب می‌کند
text: Now the math.
With a bone, in clay, a cave big enough to crouch in grows about 30 centimeters a day.
To get a meter of soil over your head, you have to go two and a half meters in.
That's eight days of work.
The asteroid hits on day ten. You have five.

see: خوابیده در گِل کنار چاله‌ی کوچک، شب
text: You dig until it's too dark to see, then sleep in the mud by the hole.
Day six. Your hands are blistered. You're in as deep as your arms can reach.
Then the roof comes down on you.
You crawl out coughing dirt.
Everything you dug, gone.
Four days left. Eight days of digging.

see: پسر نشسته در گِل، سوراخ تازه‌ی پیپ در دیواره‌ی کنار رود
text: You sit in the mud. And there, in the bank next to your ruin, a tiny new hole. Pip followed you to the river.

see: کلوز: پیپ در دهانه‌ی سوراخ کوچکش
text: His hole is tiny. And it doesn't collapse. Because Pip doesn't dig a cave. Pip digs a tunnel exactly as wide as Pip, and one small nest at the end.
So you stop digging a cave.

see: ورودی تنگ به اندازه‌ی شانه، پسر داخل می‌خزد
text: You dig a tunnel exactly as wide as your shoulders. A quarter of the dirt. Four times as fast.

see: داخل تونل: سقف قوسی با چراغ‌پیشانی
text: And you shape the roof into an arch,
because an arch pushes the weight into the walls instead of down on you.

see: ورودی کوچک گرد، پسر زانو زده
text: The entrance faces north, away from where the asteroid will hit. Maybe it makes no difference. It feels right.
Stay small. Even when you dig.

see: شب: فقط پاهای او از دهانه‌ی تنگ بیرون است
text: By dark, the tunnel swallows you to the waist.
That night you sleep with your head underground and your boots outside. It's a start.

see: پیپ جلوی ورودی، پسر از داخل
text: Day seven. Pip doesn't run anymore. He's waiting at the entrance in the morning.
You split your last chocolate with him, and you dig.

see: اینسرت: کف دست‌های زخمی روی خاک رس
text: By noon, the blisters have burst. Your palms are raw and bleeding into the clay.
And you know a hand that breaks today digs nothing tomorrow.

see: پسر به دیواره تکیه داده، خسته
text: So you stop. Even with three days left. Even if the end is coming anyway.

see: واید آرام کنار رود، پسر و پیپ
text: For one afternoon, you rest.
You switch the phone on. Just for a minute. The minute becomes an hour.
Photos. Your room.

see: عکس: مادر در آشپزخانه (روی صفحه‌ی گوشی)
text: Your mom in the kitchen.
Your friends outside school.
Then a video, from a few months ago. A class trip to a museum.

see: کلوز سلفی خندان، اسکلت پشت سر
text: You, laughing at the camera, a giant skeleton behind you.
"If they ever sent me back to the dinosaurs? I'd survive. Easy."
Your friends laughing behind the phone.
(pause)
Why are you here? What happened?
Maybe you're still asleep. Maybe this is all a dream.

see: نما از بالا: دست‌های زخمی کف‌باز
text: You look down at your hands.
The pain is real. It's not a dream.
(pause)
You always said you'd survive.
Now you have to prove it.
When you switch it off, it's at 11%. Ten percent, gone on home.
It was worth it.
That night, you fit all the way inside. You wake up, and Pip is asleep in your jacket pocket. Warm. Breathing.
Seven days in a world with no one. And now you have someone.
Day eight. You dig until your arms shake.

see: برش عرضی: تونل کامل با لانه‌ی ته
text: Two and a half meters. And at the very end, a nest, just big enough to sit up in.
A meter of soil over your head. That night, for the first time in eight days, nothing can step on you.

see: کلوز: دیوار رس و چراغ خاموش
text: (pause)
At midnight, you wake.
Scratching at the entrance. Then sniffing.
Then something coming in.
In the dark, two yellow eyes.
A feathered hunter. Fast. Only as tall as your knee.
Not a T. rex. Small enough to fit in your tunnel.
Small doesn't mean safe.
Your headlamp lights it up. It doesn't care.
It lunges. Claws rip across your right forearm.
No knife. No fire. No room to swing a bone.
Just one thing this world has never seen.
You switch the phone on. 11%.
You hit the alarm and point the flashlight straight into its face.
A sound sixty-six million years too early fills the tunnel.
It shrieks, and it's gone.
But it could come back.
Blood drips from your arm. Pip creeps out of your pocket and sits by your hand.
You can't leave the light on. It would be dead in an hour, and dawn is five hours away.

see: همان قاب، نور خاموش، فقط تاریکی و دو چشم پسر
text: So you count. Ten seconds of light. One minute of dark.
Every time the dark comes back, you listen for claws.
(pause)
When the sky turns grey, you switch it off.
Day nine. You have a fever. The wound is hot. You wrap it in a strip torn from your t-shirt.
The entrance let a hunter in. Tomorrow, it has to keep the whole world out.
One-handed, you drag stones up from the river and stack them around the opening.

see: از داخل: سنگ صاف بزرگ را مثل در می‌کشد
text: Last, a big flat stone. From inside, you can drag it across like a door, and push it aside to get out.

see: شکاف به پهنای کف دست، نور غروب از لای آن
text: When it's closed, it leaves a gap a hand wide. Enough for air. Not enough for teeth.
The sun is going down when the door slides into place.
Just in time.

see: ماهی‌های خشک روی سنگ کنار در
text: Two out of three. Twelve dried fish won't last a winter. And you're out of days.

see: کنار در سنگی، گوشی قرمز در دست (باند روی ساعد)
text: You switch the phone on one more time. The message has changed.
"Impact: tomorrow."

see: کلوز صورت خسته کنار در سنگی
text: You switch it off.
That night you slide the door aside and climb out. The sky is full of stars.

see: تی‌رکس آن طرف رود در شب
text: From across the river comes that low, familiar call. The same T. rex.
The last night of the dinosaurs. And only you know.
It isn't a strange morning. That's what makes it strange.
Birds are singing. Insects are buzzing. A few triceratops are drinking across the river.
None of them know.
Then, in the south, a light. Not like the sun.
Like someone switched the sky on by mistake.
Your book said the shaking comes within minutes. It's right.
The ground starts to move. Not like a footstep. Like the whole world.
The river pulls back. Then it comes back, the wrong way.
A wall of water runs upstream and throws fish onto the bank.

see: آب یک وجب زیر در سنگی
text: It climbs up the bank, and stops a hand below your door.
When it pulls back, you run down and grab every fish you can carry. Food for the dark.
The last thing on your list. The end of the world just handed it to you.
This isn't imagination. In North Dakota, scientists found fossil fish with tiny glass beads from this impact stuck in their gills.
Then those same glass beads start falling from the sky. Small and hot, like burning hail.
The sky turns red.

see: از داخل در سنگی را می‌کشد، پیپ در بغل
text: You drag the door shut, hold Pip tight and crawl to the end of the tunnel.
Outside, the first trees catch fire.
By evening, the whole forest is burning.
And then, outside, footsteps. Heavy. Slow. Close.
Something huge collapses at your door, and its shadow covers the gap.
The T. rex. From day one. The scar across its snout.
Its huge snout is right against the stones. Its hot breath fills your tunnel.
It can't get in. It doesn't even try.
It only came for the cool soil at your door, away from the fire.
All night, from the other side of the stones, you hear it breathing.
Each breath slower.
(pause) Until morning. (pause)
Then it stops.
The last dinosaur you saw died at your door.

see: رود گل‌آلود روی جسد تی‌رکس، فقط قسمتی بیرون
text: In the days after, the river rises again and buries the T. rex in thick mud.

see: گرافیک برش زمین: اسکلت در لایه‌ها
text: Buried fast in mud. That's how bones become fossils.
You open your book to the cover. The museum skeleton.

see: زوم به جمجمه‌ی جلد: زخم روی پوزه
text: And this time, you look closely. A long scar, healed into the bone of the snout.
(pause)
The same skeleton that stood behind you in that video. The one you joked in front of.
Sixty-six million years from now, it will stand in a museum.
And one day, you'll stand in front of it, laughing, with no idea you were here when it died.
Then the dark comes.
Soot from fires all over the world, and dust from the impact, cover the whole sky.
Sunlight can't get through. Plants can't grow. And it gets cold.
Scientists think this impact winter lasted months. Maybe years.

see: پسر با چوب سوزان از جنگل
text: The world gave you one gift on its last day. Fire. You carried an ember in from the burning forest.

see: آتش کوچک جلوی شکاف، دود بیرون
text: You keep a small fire right at the gap, never deep inside. In a closed tunnel, smoke kills quietly.
And at night, Pip sleeps against your neck. Two small bodies, keeping each other warm.
The phone won't turn on anymore. The pen is dry.
So you scratch lines on the tunnel wall with a sharp stone.
Inventory. Days after the end: 40. Still dark. Dried fish: 7. Running low. Dinosaurs left: zero. Friends: one. Mouse-sized.
You repeat the rules to yourself. Stay small. Stay near water. Stay underground.

see: پسر و پیپ دم ورودی خاکستری
text: And a new one, that no book ever taught you.
Stay small… but don't stay alone.
Small animals like Pip made it out of this darkness.
Millions of years later, from small mammals like him, came horses, whales, apes. And people.
Sixty-six million years later, one of Pip's great-great-great-grandchildren is watching this video.
And just then, from outside the tunnel, a sound. A bird, singing.
You cross out a line on the wall, and write it again.
Dinosaurs left: zero… except the birds.
On day one, what would you have done first? Tell me in the comments.
And if you want to know what you and Pip did after the dark, tell me that too.
Stay small. Stay alive.
